jobs.title: Director of Engineering
jobs.description:
Summary

The Director of Engineering provides strategic leadership for engineering, maintenance, facilities, and reliability initiatives across multiple corrugated manufacturing plants. This position develops a unified maintenance and asset reliability strategy, aligns engineering resources across facilities, and ensures maintenance efforts are coordinated to maximize equipment availability, safety, productivity, and cost effectiveness. The role partners closely with plant leadership to standardize best practices, prioritize capital improvements, and drive continuous improvement across the enterprise.

Duties And Responsibilities

Develop and execute an annual enterprise-wide engineering, maintenance, and reliability strategy with defined targets for uptime, maintenance cost, planned maintenance compliance, safety, and capital project execution.
Develop, manage, and meet an annual maintenance and engineering budget to include capital investment, maintenance and repair vendors, asset replacement, and internal labor cost. This will be measured in part through overall effect on revenue, EBITA, and year-over-year ROI on the business
Standardize preventive, predictive, and reliability-centered maintenance programs across all facilities, including common preventative maintenance compliance targets, inspection standards, and CMMS reporting requirements.
Act as a key member of the Operations leadership team providing counsel to the VP of Operations and C-Suite leaders on all aspects of maintenance, reliability, and engineering
Coordinate engineering resources and maintenance priorities to complete approved enterprise initiatives on schedule, within budget, and according to defined operational requirements.
Establish, monitor, and report monthly KPIs for equipment uptime, maintenance costs, PM compliance, asset reliability, MTBF, MTTR, and maintenance backlog to drive continuous improvement.
Provide executive oversight of enterprise root cause analyses (RCAs) for significant equipment failures and implement sustainable corrective actions ensuring corrective actions are implemented, validated, and recurrence rates are reduced through documented follow-up.
Partner with Operations to improve equipment performance, throughput, safety, and product quality using agreed-upon metrics such as downtime, OEE, scrap, safety incidents, and customer quality defects
Oversee enterprise-wide capital planning for equipment modernization and engineering support for major projects, including capital roadmap from business case through design, vendor selection, installation, commissioning, startup, and post-project performance
Champion a culture of continuous improvement across all engineering and maintenance functions by standardizing maintenance planning, CMMS governance, reliability processes, and performance management practices. Utilize enterprise maintenance and reliability metrics to identify opportunities, eliminate inefficiencies, reduce reactive maintenance, improve asset performance, and drive operational excellence across all manufacturing facilities.
Ensure compliance with applicable safety, environmental, and engineering standards, measured by audit results, corrective-action closure rates, regulatory findings, incident trends, and timely resolution of identified deficiencies.
Build organizational capability, measured by completion of annual succession plans, leadership development goals, technical training completion rates, bench-strength assessments, retention of key roles, and improvement against workforce capability gaps.
Special projects and assignments as business dictates
Responsible for the maintenance, creation and control of all personally identifiable information or any other information protected by any Confidentiality or Privacy Standards or Company Policies that you have access or knowledge of, including but not limited to any state or federal regulations including HIPAA

Supervisory Responsibilities

Director of Facilities and Maintenance
Assistant Maintenance Manager
Maintenance Manager

Skills And Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Engineering or related technical field required. Master’s degree in a related field preferred.
12+ years of progressive engineering and maintenance leadership experience in manufacturing required.
Experience in corrugated packaging or related high-volume manufacturing required.
Strong knowledge of reliability-centered maintenance, TPM, predictive maintenance, CMMS, and asset management required.
Experience leading multi-site engineering or maintenance organizations required.
Knowledge of capital project management and equipment lifecycle planning.
Excellent leadership, communication, and cross-functional collaboration skills.
Must have attention to detail and focused concentration.
Must be able to learn new tasks and complete tasks independently.
Must be able to make timely decisions in the context of the workflow.
Must possess strong organizational skills, ability to multi-task and responsiveness.

PHYSICAL DEMANDS

Regularly required to stand, walk, climb, kneel, crouch, and crawl during plant visits.
Occasionally lift and/or move up to 50 pounds.
Reasonable accommodation may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

WORK ENVIRONMENT

Frequent travel between multiple corrugated manufacturing facilities.
Regular exposure to manufacturing environments with moving mechanical equipment, noise, dust, and varying temperatures.
Hearing protection required in production areas.

CERTIFICATES, LICENSES, REGISTRATIONS

Professional Engineer (PE) license preferred.
Certified Maintenance & Reliability Professional (CMRP) preferred.
Lean Six Sigma certification preferred.

Other Duties

Please note this job description is not designed to cover or contain a comprehensive listing of activities, duties or responsibilities that are required of the employee for this job. Duties, responsibilities and activities may change at any time with or without notice.

jobs.title: Sr. Manager, Vehicle EOL Integration and Test Engineering
jobs.description:
About Rivian

Rivian is on a mission to keep the world adventurous forever. This goes for the emissions-free Electric Adventure Vehicles we build, and the curious, courageous souls we seek to attract.

As a company, we constantly challenge what’s possible, never simply accepting what has always been done. We reframe old problems, seek new solutions and operate comfortably in areas that are unknown. Our backgrounds are diverse, but our team shares a love of the outdoors and a desire to protect it for future generations.

Role Summary

Rivian is seeking a Sr. Manager, Vehicle EOL Integration & Test Engineering to lead the organization responsible for integrating vehicle functionality, factory systems, and comprehensive test capabilities into a robust production environment. This leader will bridge vehicle engineering, manufacturing engineering, controls, quality, operations, and service teams to ensure every vehicle is functionally validated and ready to ship.

The ideal candidate is a hands-on technical and people leader who can translate complex vehicle and factory requirements into scalable end-of-line test strategies, resilient functional integration processes, and disciplined launch execution. This role is based on-site in Normal, Illinois and requires close partnership with factory leadership and cross-functional engineering teams.

Responsibilities

Lead and develop a team of managers and engineers responsible for factory functional test integration, validation systems, diagnostics, and production readiness
Own the strategy and execution of functional testing across vehicle build, commissioning, end-of-line, rework, and audit processes
Establish factory functional testing standards spanning vehicle configuration, systems validation, diagnostics, test sequencing, traceability, and data capture
Partner with Vehicle Engineering and Software teams to convert design intent and test requirements into manufacturable, repeatable production processes
Drive launch readiness for new vehicle programs, major software and system updates, plant changes, and process upgrades, including validation plans, cutover plans, and issue containment
Define and manage requirements for test equipment, fixtures, automation, network interfaces, manufacturing execution systems, and production data infrastructure
Create a closed-loop approach to test failures by improving fault isolation, diagnostic coverage, repair guidance, retest logic, and feedback to engineering
Lead cross-functional resolution of complex functional, controls, and manufacturing issues, balancing production continuity with long-term corrective action
Establish technical reviews, change-control processes, release criteria, and escalation mechanisms that protect safety, quality, throughput, and customer experience
Use production data and manufacturing analytics to identify test escapes, recurring failure modes, cycle-time opportunities, and process capability improvements Ensure processes and systems meet applicable safety, quality, cybersecurity, traceability, and change-management expectations
Build strong relationships with Operations, Quality, Supply Chain, IT/OT, Service, and external equipment and technology partners

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Software Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, or a related technical field; advanced degree is a plus
10+ years of experience in automotive, aerospace, industrial automation, electronics manufacturing, or a comparable complex production environment
5+ years of experience leading technical teams, including managers and senior engineers
Demonstrated experience with vehicle systems validation, diagnostics, end-of-line testing, or comprehensive manufacturing test systems
Experience launching or scaling production systems in a high-volume manufacturing environment
Strong understanding of test strategy, requirements management, configuration control, defect triage, and production data analysis
Experience integrating factory test systems and equipment with vehicle platforms, manufacturing execution systems, databases, or plant networks
Ability to lead through ambiguity, make timely decisions, and communicate effectively with both technical and executive audiences
Willingness to work on-site in Normal, Illinois and support production launches, critical issue resolution, and occasional off-shift activities when needed

Preferred Qualifications

Experience with automotive manufacturing, vehicle systems validation, diagnostics, or functional commissioning
Experience with CAN, LIN, Ethernet, UDS, or similar vehicle communication and diagnostic protocols
Familiarity with automated test equipment, National Instruments or comparable platforms, PLC/controls integration, and industrial networking
Experience with manufacturing execution systems, test databases, cloud-connected production data, or digital traceability
Working knowledge of software development practices, APIs, version control, CI/CD concepts, and release management
Experience applying Lean, Six Sigma, statistical process control, or structured problem-solving methods
Track record of leading new product introduction, plant transformation, or major factory test system deployments

Salary Range for Illinois Based Applicants:
The salary range for this position is $161,000 - $201,200 for Illinois based applicants. This is the lowest to highest salary we in good faith believe we would pay for this role at the time of this posting. An employee’s position within the salary range will be based on several factors including, but not limited to, specific competencies, relevant education, qualifications, certifications, experience, skills, geographic location, shift, and organizational needs.

The successful candidate may be eligible for annual performance bonus and equity awards.

We offer a comprehensive package of benefits for full-time and part-time employees, their spouse or domestic partner, and children up to age 26, including but not limited to paid vacation, paid sick leave, and a competitive portfolio of insurance benefits including life, medical, dental, vision, short-term disability insurance, and long-term disability insurance to eligible employees. Join Western Union as a Director, Software Engineering.

Experience with containerized microservices, Kubernetes, and modern API platforms.

Job Title:
Director, Technology Strategy & Enablement

Department
: Technology Services

Company:
Southern Company Services

Reports To:
Vice President, Technology Services

Job Summary

Southern Company Services is seeking a Director of Technology Strategy & Enablement to lead the Technology Organization's horizontal strategy function. This role is responsible for developing the overarching technology strategy, multi-year capability roadmaps, technology OKRs, and value realization framework that enable Southern Company's business and transformation objectives.

Operating across the Technology Organization, this leader will aggregate demand and strategic requirements from Electric, Gas, Enterprise, and Shared Services portfolios to identify common capability needs, strategic dependencies, and opportunities for platform reuse and standardization. Working closely with Architecture, Infrastructure & Cloud Engineering, Cybersecurity, Data & AI, and Application leaders, the Director will help ensure foundational technology capabilities are planned, aligned, and available to support future business needs.

This role serves as a strategic enabler and connector across the Technology Organization. It is accountable for technology strategy, capability planning, alignment, and value measurement. It does not own project delivery, portfolio execution governance, application business ownership, or investment approval authority.

Major Job Responsibilities

Lead the Technology Organization's strategic planning process and translate enterprise priorities into a cohesive technology strategy and multi-year capability roadmap.
Partner with business strategy, operating company, and functional leadership teams to translate business objectives, growth strategies, regulatory requirements, and operational priorities into technology capabilities, roadmaps, and investment recommendations.
Lead strategic assessments and recommendations for the Technology Organization operating model, including organizational capabilities, governance, sourcing strategies, workforce planning, and service delivery models required to support future business needs.
Aggregate demand across technology portfolios to identify shared foundational capabilities, strategic dependencies, and opportunities for reuse, standardization, and cost optimization.
Develop and maintain 3-5 year technology capability roadmaps that support business transformation, modernization, and innovation objectives.
Partner with Enterprise Architecture, Infrastructure & Cloud Engineering, Cybersecurity, Data & AI, and Application leadership to align technology strategies and investment priorities.
Identify technology capability gaps, platform overlap, technical debt reduction opportunities, and future-state enablement requirements.
Establish and manage Technology Organization OKRs, executive scorecards, and dashboards that measure strategic progress, organizational performance, and value realization.
Translate strategic priorities into roadmap recommendations, investment themes, and executive decision support materials.
Support technology investment planning by providing strategic insights, capability requirements, business outcome alignment, and expected value realization.
Partner with PMO, Application VPs, and business stakeholders to ensure alignment between technology strategy, portfolio priorities, and execution plans while maintaining clear ownership within each organization.
Drive visibility and transparency into Technology Organization performance, ensuring leaders can effectively measure outcomes, business value, and strategic impact.

Knowledge And Skills

Leadership, Change & People Management

Transformational Leadership & Talent Development: Recognized as a change agent who challenges the status quo. Demonstrated ability to attract top talent, build high-performing teams, and lead with well-defined core values.
A Proactive, "Business-First" Mentality: Applies sound business judgment to "connect the dots," with a relentless focus on removing friction, clearing roadblocks, and partnering with the business to accelerate transformation.

Influence, Collaboration & Communication

Executive Influence & EQ: High emotional intelligence with outstanding credibility. Demonstrated ability to influence senior management
Exceptional Communication: Superb written and verbal communication skills, with extensive experiencepresenting to, advising, and building strong relationships with executive leadership, steering committees, and key vendors.

Strategic Technology & Portfolio Capabilities

Enterprise Portfolio & Financial Acumen: Demonstratedability to manage large-scale technology investment portfolios,establish capability roadmaps, and define value-realization frameworks (such as OKRs) to track technology ROI.
Strategic Technology & AI Fluency: Strong conceptual understanding of modern technology paradigms—specifically Cloud architectures, Data Platforms (e.g., Databricks), AI/MLOps, and high-density Telecom—with the ability to translate complex concepts into business outcomes.
Horizontal Capability Synthesis: Proven success in aggregating fragmented technology demands from multiple business units (e.g., Power Delivery, Gas, Customer Service) into unified, shared-platform strategies to prevent redundant investments.
Tech-for-Tech Strategy Facilitation: Demonstratedability to partner with core engineering leaders tofacilitatelong-term strategic roadmaps for back-end technical functions (Infrastructure, platforms) to reduce technical debt.

Education

Bachelor's degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, Engineering, Business, or related field; advanced degree preferred.
MBA or Master’s degree (e.g., MS in Technology Management or Information Systems) is highly preferred.

Experience

10+ years of progressive leadership experience in technology strategy, enterprise architecture, portfolio management, technology consulting, or related disciplines.
Demonstrated success developing enterprise technology strategies, capability roadmaps, and value realization frameworks.
Experience establishing OKRs, executive scorecards, and performance measurement programs.
Demonstrated experience shaping strategies for modern data environments, AI enablement, cloud transformations, and proactive enterprise security protocols.
Extensive experience interfacing with non-technical business executives, representing IT on steering committees, and driving consensus across highly matrixed, cross-functional organizations.
Experience operating within large, complex, regulated organizations.

Leadership Competencies

Strategic and enterprise thinker
Trusted advisor and relationship builder
Strong business and financial acumen
Executive presence and stakeholder influence
Collaborative leadership style with high emotional intelligence
Ability to translate strategy into measurable business outcomes

About Southern Company

Southern Company (NYSE: SO ) is a leading energy provider serving 9 million customers across the Southeast and beyond through its family of companies. Providing clean, safe, reliable and affordable energy with excellent service is our mission. The company has electric operating companies in three states, natural gas distribution companies in four states, a competitive generation company, a leading distributed energy solutions provider with national capabilities, a fiber optics network and telecommunications services. Through an industry-leading commitment to innovation, resilience and sustainability, we are taking action to meet customers' and communities' needs while advancing our goal of net-zero greenhouse gas emissions by 2050. Our uncompromising values ensure we put the needs of those we serve at the center of everything we do and are the key to our sustained success. We are transforming energy into economic, environmental and social progress for tomorrow. Our corporate culture has been recognized by a variety of organizations, earning the company awards and recognitions that reflect Our Values and dedication to service. To learn more, visit www.southerncompany.com .

Southern Company invests in the well-being of its employees and their families through a comprehensive total rewards strategy that includes competitive base salary, annual incentive awards for eligible employees and health, welfare and retirement benefits designed to support physical, financial, and emotional/social well-being. This position may also be eligible for additional compensation, such as an incentive program, with the amount of any bonus/awards subject to the terms and conditions of the applicable incentive plan(s). A summary of the benefits offered for this position can be found here https://seo.nlx.org/southernco/pdf/SOCO-Benefits.pdf . Additional and specific details about total compensation and beneﬁts will also be provided during the hiring process.

Job Summary

Southern Company Services is seeking a Director of Technology Strategy & Enablement to lead the Technology Organization's horizontal strategy function. This role is responsible for developing the overarching technology strategy, multi-year capability roadmaps, technology OKRs, and value realization framework that enable Southern Company's business and transformation objectives.

Operating across the Technology Organization, this leader will aggregate demand and strategic requirements from Electric, Gas, Enterprise, and Shared Services portfolios to identify common capability needs, strategic dependencies, and opportunities for platform reuse and standardization. Working closely with Architecture, Infrastructure & Cloud Engineering, Cybersecurity, Data & AI, and Application leaders, the Director will help ensure foundational technology capabilities are planned, aligned, and available to support future business needs.

This role serves as a strategic enabler and connector across the Technology Organization. It is accountable for technology strategy, capability planning, alignment, and value measurement. It does not own project delivery, portfolio execution governance, application business ownership, or investment approval authority.

Major Job Responsibilities

Lead the Technology Organization's strategic planning process and translate enterprise priorities into a cohesive technology strategy and multi-year capability roadmap.
Partner with business strategy, operating company, and functional leadership teams to translate business objectives, growth strategies, regulatory requirements, and operational priorities into technology capabilities, roadmaps, and investment recommendations.
Lead strategic assessments and recommendations for the Technology Organization operating model, including organizational capabilities, governance, sourcing strategies, workforce planning, and service delivery models required to support future business needs.
Aggregate demand across technology portfolios to identify shared foundational capabilities, strategic dependencies, and opportunities for reuse, standardization, and cost optimization.
Develop and maintain 3-5 year technology capability roadmaps that support business transformation, modernization, and innovation objectives.
Partner with Enterprise Architecture, Infrastructure & Cloud Engineering, Cybersecurity, Data & AI, and Application leadership to align technology strategies and investment priorities.
Identify technology capability gaps, platform overlap, technical debt reduction opportunities, and future-state enablement requirements.
Establish and manage Technology Organization OKRs, executive scorecards, and dashboards that measure strategic progress, organizational performance, and value realization.
Translate strategic priorities into roadmap recommendations, investment themes, and executive decision support materials.
Support technology investment planning by providing strategic insights, capability requirements, business outcome alignment, and expected value realization.
Partner with PMO, Application VPs, and business stakeholders to ensure alignment between technology strategy, portfolio priorities, and execution plans while maintaining clear ownership within each organization.
Drive visibility and transparency into Technology Organization performance, ensuring leaders can effectively measure outcomes, business value, and strategic impact.

Knowledge And Skills

Leadership, Change & People Management

Transformational Leadership & Talent Development: Recognized as a change agent who challenges the status quo. Demonstrated ability to attract top talent, build high-performing teams, and lead with well-defined core values.
A Proactive, "Business-First" Mentality: Applies sound business judgment to "connect the dots," with a relentless focus on removing friction, clearing roadblocks, and partnering with the business to accelerate transformation.

Influence, Collaboration & Communication

Executive Influence & EQ: High emotional intelligence with outstanding credibility. Demonstrated ability to influence senior management
Exceptional Communication: Superb written and verbal communication skills, with extensive experiencepresenting to, advising, and building strong relationships with executive leadership, steering committees, and key vendors.

Strategic Technology & Portfolio Capabilities

Enterprise Portfolio & Financial Acumen: Demonstratedability to manage large-scale technology investment portfolios,establish capability roadmaps, and define value-realization frameworks (such as OKRs) to track technology ROI.
Strategic Technology & AI Fluency: Strong conceptual understanding of modern technology paradigms—specifically Cloud architectures, Data Platforms (e.g., Databricks), AI/MLOps, and high-density Telecom—with the ability to translate complex concepts into business outcomes.
Horizontal Capability Synthesis: Proven success in aggregating fragmented technology demands from multiple business units (e.g., Power Delivery, Gas, Customer Service) into unified, shared-platform strategies to prevent redundant investments.
Tech-for-Tech Strategy Facilitation: Demonstratedability to partner with core engineering leaders tofacilitatelong-term strategic roadmaps for back-end technical functions (Infrastructure, platforms) to reduce technical debt.

Education

Bachelor's degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, Engineering, Business, or related field; advanced degree preferred.
MBA or Master’s degree (e.g., MS in Technology Management or Information Systems) is highly preferred.

Experience

10+ years of progressive leadership experience in technology strategy, enterprise architecture, portfolio management, technology consulting, or related disciplines.
Demonstrated success developing enterprise technology strategies, capability roadmaps, and value realization frameworks.
Experience establishing OKRs, executive scorecards, and performance measurement programs.
Demonstrated experience shaping strategies for modern data environments, AI enablement, cloud transformations, and proactive enterprise security protocols.
Extensive experience interfacing with non-technical business executives, representing IT on steering committees, and driving consensus across highly matrixed, cross-functional organizations.
Experience operating within large, complex, regulated organizations.

Leadership Competencies

Strategic and enterprise thinker
Trusted advisor and relationship builder
Strong business and financial acumen
Executive presence and stakeholder influence
Collaborative leadership style with high emotional intelligence
Ability to translate strategy into measurable business outcomes

Southern Company (NYSE: SO ) is a leading energy provider serving 9 million customers across the Southeast and beyond through its family of companies. Providing clean, safe, reliable and affordable energy with excellent service is our mission. The company has electric operating companies in three states, natural gas distribution companies in four states, a competitive generation company, a leading distributed energy solutions provider with national capabilities, a fiber optics network and telecommunications services. Through an industry-leading commitment to innovation, resilience and sustainability, we are taking action to meet customers' and communities' needs while advancing our goal of net-zero greenhouse gas emissions by 2050. Our uncompromising values ensure we put the needs of those we serve at the center of everything we do and are the key to our sustained success. We are transforming energy into economic, environmental and social progress for tomorrow. Our corporate culture has been recognized by a variety of organizations, earning the company awards and recognitions that reflect Our Values and dedication to service. To learn more, visit www.southerncompany.com .

Southern Company invests in the well-being of its employees and their families through a comprehensive total rewards strategy that includes competitive base salary, annual incentive awards for eligible employees and health, welfare and retirement benefits designed to support physical, financial, and emotional/social well-being.
